input_signals.name: Cash-Validated Intangible Spending
input_signals.hypothesis: High R&D and advertising intensity should predict higher returns only when operating cash flow is sufficient to cover short-term debt.
input_signals.reasoning: R&D and advertising can create valuable unrecognized capital, but aggressive spending is dangerous when refinancing needs exceed internally generated cash. The cash-coverage condition separates financially sustainable intangible investment from spending undertaken under genuine funding pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), sale ) ), indicator( sub( oancf, dlc ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Knowledge-Weighted Cash-Coverage Stability
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with stable operating-cash-flow coverage of current liabilities should outperform R&D-intensive firms whose coverage is unstable.
input_signals.reasoning: Volatile cash coverage is evidence of genuine funding fragility because knowledge investment requires continuity and offers limited liquidation value. The signed interaction rewards stability and penalizes instability primarily among R&D-intensive firms, without restricting the signal to a sparse negative-equity or retained-deficit subset.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ), neg( ind_zscore( winsor( vol( ratio( oancf, lct ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D-Weighted Short-Debt Cash Surplus
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D intensity should predict higher returns when operating cash flow exceeds short-term debt, but lower returns when the same knowledge investment accompanies a cash funding deficit.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the prior binary cash-validation gate with a signed, continuous measure, reducing ties and allowing cash-short R&D firms to form an economically meaningful short leg. Omitting advertising also avoids treating nonreported advertising as a verified zero while preserving the previously successful cash-validation mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, dlc ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Two-Year Coverage Floor
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MIN(RATIO(oancf, lct), LAG(RATIO(oancf, lct), 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms with adequate cash-flow coverage in both the current and previous period should outperform firms whose knowledge investment coincides with even one period of severe coverage weakness.
input_signals.reasoning: The two-period minimum measures the persistent downside floor of operating cash coverage rather than volatility, which can be high for successful growth firms as well as distressed firms. Using one lag should retain more coverage than a long volatility window while producing more stable portfolio assignments than a contemporaneous indicator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( min( ratio( oancf, lct ), lag( ratio( oancf, lct ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Pre-R&D Earnings Distress Separator
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms reporting weak income, strong earnings before current R&D investment relative to liabilities should indicate accounting distress and predict higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding R&D to income estimates earnings capacity before discretionary knowledge investment without claiming that R&D is a noncash expense. Reported-loss severity concentrates the signal where reclassification matters, while signed adjusted coverage separates firms capable of funding knowledge creation from firms that remain unprofitable before R&D.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ratio( ib, at ) ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Recognized-Intangible Cash Insolvency
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms concentrated in recognized intangible assets should underperform when operating cash flow provides weak or negative coverage of total liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Separately recognized intangibles offer uncertain liquidation value, but they become a genuine solvency concern only when operations fail to generate cash against creditor claims. This nonlinear joint-state construction replaces the additive soft-assets-minus-equity measure and uses operating cash coverage rather than reusing the archived short-term maturity gap.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( oancf, lt ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Dual-Failure Fragility
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(oancf, lt)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms should underperform when both earnings before current R&D and post-R&D operating cash flow provide weak liability coverage.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding back R&D tests whether reported losses remain after removing current knowledge investment, while operating cash flow tests actual financing capacity after that spending. The minimum of the two fragility ranks becomes large only when both tests confirm weakness, reducing false distress classifications driven by accounting alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ), min( rank( winsor( neg( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( oancf, lt ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D-Adjusted Gross-Surplus Coverage
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sale, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms whose gross surplus remains strong after deducting R&D and scaling by liabilities should outperform firms whose product economics cannot support their knowledge spending.
input_signals.reasoning: Subtracting R&D from gross profit removes the mechanical gross-margin advantage created because R&D is recorded outside cost of goods sold. The resulting liability coverage tests whether product-market surplus can support both knowledge investment and creditor claims.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sale, cogs ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Recognized-Intangible Earnings Insolvency
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms concentrated in recognized intangible assets should underperform when they remain unprofitable relative to liabilities even before current R&D spending.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding back current R&D prevents ordinary knowledge investment from mechanically creating the earnings failure used to classify distress. The interaction instead tests whether recognized intangible assets are supported by underlying earnings capacity, providing an earnings-based complement to the successful cash-insolvency mechanism with broader expected coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Leveraged Goodwill Cash Failure
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(oancf, lt)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that are jointly goodwill-intensive and highly leveraged should underperform when operating cash flow provides weak coverage of liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Weak cash coverage is a direct financial-fragility test that avoids relying on the ambiguous return implications of sales contraction. The minimum operator requires meaningful exposure to both goodwill and leverage before cash failure receives substantial weight, targeting debt-financed acquisition value that operations cannot support.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 1 ) ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( oancf, lt ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D-Capitalization Leverage Relief
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose leverage ranking falls substantially after recognizing accumulated R&D as knowledge capital should earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The expression directly compares reported leverage with a counterfactual leverage ratio that augments assets by cumulative R&D, eliminating the sales-to-assets channel that confounded the prior scaling-gap proposal. A large positive rank reduction therefore measures accounting leverage inflation specifically attributable to omitted knowledge capital rather than generic operating efficiency.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( lt, at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( lt, add( at, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Earnings-Validated R&D Leverage Relief
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(SUB(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(lt, at), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(lt, ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3))), 1)))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D capitalization should indicate overstated accounting leverage only when the underlying business also generates adequate earnings before current R&D relative to liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: The original capitalization-relief signal had a positive cross-sectional slope but negative portfolio alpha, consistent with its high tail including firms whose accumulated R&D was unproductive. The minimum operator requires both material leverage relief and current earnings validation, aiming to remove those firms without imposing a sparse indicator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( sub( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( lt, at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( lt, add( at, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ) ) ), 1 ) ) ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Sheltered Knowledge Volatility
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), lt), 3), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dlc), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with volatile gross-surplus coverage should earn higher returns when operating cash flow nevertheless covers short-term debt.
input_signals.reasoning: The archived gross-surplus-instability signal generated positive rather than hypothesized negative alpha, suggesting that volatility may represent innovation optionality rather than fragility. Requiring a contemporaneous cash surplus separates financially sheltered upside uncertainty from volatility accompanied by refinancing pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ), min( rank( winsor( vol( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), lt ), 3 ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, dlc ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Goodwill Historical Earnings Support
input_signals.hypothesis: Goodwill-intensive firms with sustained earnings coverage of liabilities should outperform goodwill-intensive firms whose acquired business value is accompanied by persistent losses.
input_signals.reasoning: A multi-period earnings state tests whether acquired operations have generated durable accounting returns, rather than swapping another contemporaneous coverage numerator into the goodwill cash-failure template. Smoothing also reduces the influence of a single impairment charge or transitory earnings observation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ma( ratio( ib, lt ), 3 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Tax-Profit Confirmation
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(pi, lt), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(txt, lt), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms that generate both positive pretax income and a positive tax provision relative to liabilities should outperform firms whose knowledge spending lacks taxable-profit confirmation.
input_signals.reasoning: Pretax income and the associated tax provision provide a distinct validation channel that does not rely on operating cash flow, accrual gaps, or gross-surplus substitutions. Requiring both reduces the chance that unusual tax items alone classify an R&D-intensive firm as financially resilient.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ), min( rank( winsor( ratio( pi, lt ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( txt, lt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent Knowledge Burden Under Core Loss
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with a persistently high R&D commitment should underperform when they remain unprofitable relative to liabilities even before current R&D expense.
input_signals.reasoning: The historical R&D floor measures a quasi-fixed knowledge-investment burden rather than dispersion or recovery in gross surplus. Weak earnings after adding back current R&D then confirms that the firm cannot resolve its distress simply by reducing knowledge spending.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), lt ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Joint Book Distress Knowledge Coverage
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that appear weak on book equity but possess substantial accumulated R&D relative to liabilities should earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The prior signed interaction produced portfolio alpha without a monotone cross-sectional slope, suggesting that its opposing tails were difficult to order. This joint-state score is high only when conventional book distress and knowledge-capital claim coverage coexist, directly targeting accounting misclassification rather than ranking R&D coverage alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( winsor( neg( ratio( ceq, at ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), lt ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Knowledge Commercialization Claim Efficiency
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with substantial accumulated R&D should outperform when revenue is high relative to the combined scale of creditor claims and the knowledge-capital proxy.
input_signals.reasoning: The first leg requires material knowledge intensity, while the second measures commercialization output per unit of knowledge investment and liabilities. This is not rank-equivalent to R&D divided by liabilities because revenue enters as an independent realized-output channel.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), at ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( revt, add( lt, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent Knowledge Retained-Earnings Replenishment
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms sustaining high R&D intensity should outperform when retained earnings relative to liabilities are improving and underperform when accumulated capital is deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: Persistent R&D identifies a continuing knowledge strategy, while the retained-earnings trend measures whether that strategy is replenishing cumulative equity rather than consuming it. This avoids cash-flow, accrual-gap, and tax-loss conditioners and gives the two signal tails opposite cumulative-capital interpretations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( trend( ratio( re, lt ), 3 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Recognized-Intangible Gross Claim Productivity
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), ADD(lt, COALESCE(intan, 0))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with substantial recognized intangible assets should outperform when gross surplus is high relative to liabilities and the recognized intangible stock.
input_signals.reasoning: Strong cash- and earnings-insolvency results show that recognized intangibles are risky when unsupported, but they do not test whether those assets generate product-level surplus. This signal directly measures commercialization productivity while requiring economically meaningful intangible exposure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), add( lt, coalesce( intan, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent Knowledge Revenue Floor
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms sustaining substantial R&D should outperform when revenue coverage of liabilities also remains strong across the same horizon.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal tests whether a durable knowledge commitment is supported by a durable top-line operating base, rather than adding another debt term to an earnings-loss signal. Using downside floors for both channels distinguishes persistent commercialization capacity from a single strong revenue or R&D observation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ts_min( ratio( revt, lt ), 3 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Deficit-State Goodwill Revenue Realization
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(re, at)), 1))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(revt, ADD(lt, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among goodwill-intensive firms with weak accumulated retained earnings, strong revenue relative to liabilities and goodwill should predict higher returns, while weak revenue should confirm genuine acquisition-related fragility.
input_signals.reasoning: Goodwill and retained-earnings weakness identify firms where acquired value lacks an accumulated profit cushion, while revenue realization supplies a separate commercialization test. This construction avoids the archived cash, earnings-coverage, tax-loss, and goodwill-versus-R&D contrast channels.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( re, at ) ), 1 ) ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( revt, add( lt, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Validated Knowledge Commercialization
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(revt, ADD(lt, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3))), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dlc), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with substantial accumulated R&D should outperform when knowledge commercialization is strong and operating cash flow also covers short-term debt.
input_signals.reasoning: Revenue-based commercialization produced the strongest cross-sectional result among the knowledge-stock signals, but booked revenue need not provide near-term financing capacity. Requiring both claim-adjusted revenue and a cash surplus targets productive knowledge capital that is commercially successful and financially self-sustaining.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), at ) ), min( rank( winsor( ratio( revt, add( lt, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ) ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, dlc ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Converted Deficit Goodwill Realization
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(re, at)), 1))), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(revt, ADD(lt, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dlc), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Goodwill-intensive firms with accumulated deficits should outperform when acquired business value generates both strong revenue and sufficient cash to cover short-term debt.
input_signals.reasoning: The revenue-realization signal generated a strong slope but only moderate alpha, suggesting that some high-revenue firms failed to convert commercialization into financing capacity. Joint revenue and cash validation separates productive acquired intangibles from goodwill supported only by accounting sales.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( re, at ) ), 1 ) ) ), min( rank( winsor( ratio( revt, add( lt, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, dlc ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with persistent R&D commitments should underperform when they are both unprofitable before current R&D and inefficient at converting accumulated knowledge into revenue.
input_signals.reasoning: Persistent R&D combined with core loss already identified genuine fragility, but some loss-making firms may still possess commercially productive knowledge options.
